* [Delivery nodes](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/canvas/nodes/delivery.md): Send creative to the Planner, a platform, or a Meta ad.

## Try it

Make one image per headline with a **Batch** node:

1. Right-click the canvas, choose **Add Node**, and type `Batch` in **Search nodes…**.
2. Add your five headlines to the Batch list.
3. Connect the Batch output to the prompt of an **Image Generation** node.
4. Choose **Run Flow**. The generator runs once for each headline.

Or ask Claude or ChatGPT to build it for you:

* "On my open canvas, make one square image for each of these five headlines: …"
* "Add an image generator to my open canvas, connect it to the product photo, and run just that node."

## What's next

* [Models](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/canvas/models.md): The image and video models generation nodes use.
* [Skills and grounding](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/canvas/skills-and-grounding.md): Keep every generation on-brand.

# Image nodes

Source: https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/canvas/nodes/image

> Generate images, and bring in image references, Elements, your design system, and composed layers.

Image nodes live in the **Image** section of the **Add Node** menu. Use them to generate stills and to feed references into other generators.

## Image generation

The **Image Generation** node generates images with the model you choose.

**Inputs → outputs:** a prompt, an optional negative prompt, reference images, and a trigger → up to 4 image variations.

**1. Add the node**

Right-click the canvas, choose **Add Node → Image**, and pick **Image Generation**.

**2. Pick a model**

Choose a model and its size or aspect ratio. See [Models](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/canvas/models.md).

**3. Connect inputs**

Wire in a prompt from a [Text Block](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/canvas/nodes/text-audio-documents.md), and any reference images or Elements.

**4. Run**

Select **Run Node**, or run the whole graph with **Run Flow**.

## Image reference

The **Image Reference** node brings an image file onto the canvas as an input.

**Inputs → outputs:** none → image.

## Element

A saved model, product, character, or style, used as a reusable reference. Wire it into a generator so the subject looks the same in everything you make. An Element doesn't generate anything itself.

**Inputs → outputs:** none → image (or video, for a motion Element).

See [Elements](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/canvas/elements.md) to create and manage them.

## Design reference

**Design Reference** node: one section of your brand's design system, as a live reference. Select **Generate** (or **Regenerate**) to build a specimen of that section.

**Inputs → outputs:** none → an image specimen and the section's tokens as text.

## Layer editor

**Layer Editor** node: stacks, places, and blends stills into one composed image.

**Inputs → outputs:** images → image.

## Try it

Ask Claude or ChatGPT:

* "Make four square images of our cold brew can on a marble counter in morning light."
* "Use our hero product Element for three new lifestyle images."

On the canvas, connect a product photo as an **Image Reference** to an **Image Generation** node, write the scene in a **Text Block**, and choose **Run Node**.

## What's next

* [Models](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/canvas/models.md): Image models, sizes, and aspect ratios.
* [Video nodes](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/canvas/nodes/video.md): Turn stills into clips.

# Video nodes

Source: https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/canvas/nodes/video

> Generate clips, edit them into variations, extend footage, break video down, and open it in Video Studio.

Video nodes live in the **Video** section of the **Add Node** menu.

## Video generation

The **Video Generation** node generates a clip with a video model. The menu lists one row per model, so you pick the model as you add the node. See [Models](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/canvas/models.md) for each model's options.

**Inputs → outputs:** a prompt plus reference images or frames, depending on the model → video.

## Omni 1.1 Flash (Edit)

Generates a clip, then lets you chat to edit, extend, and upscale it into variations.

**Inputs → outputs:** a prompt, reference images, and a reference video → video.

## Extend video

The **Extend Video** node continues existing footage.

**Inputs → outputs:** a prompt and a video → video.

## Video decoder

The **Video Decoder** node breaks a video down frame by frame for creative analysis.

**Inputs → outputs:** video → text.

## Video editor

**Video Editor** node: a full editor to trim, split, and sequence clips and stills. It opens [Video Studio](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/canvas/video-studio.md).

**Inputs → outputs:** a pool of media → video.

## HyperFrames agent

The **HyperFrames Agent** node creates video with an agent that builds it in HTML, using your media as references.

**Inputs → outputs:** a prompt and up to 20 images, videos, or audio files → video.

## Video reference

The **Video Reference** node brings a video file onto the canvas as an input.

**Inputs → outputs:** none → video.

## Try it

Ask Claude or ChatGPT:

* "Turn this product photo into a vertical video clip for Reels."
* "Make an 8-second 9:16 clip of our cold brew being poured over ice, using our hero product Element."

On the canvas, add **Extend Video** from the **Video** section, connect your clip and a **Text Block** that reads "slow push-in on the label", and choose **Run Node** to continue the shot.

## What's next

* [Models](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/canvas/models.md): Video models, resolutions, and durations.
* [Video Studio](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/canvas/video-studio.md): Cut, caption, and export.

# Text, audio, and document nodes

Source: https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/canvas/nodes/text-audio-documents

> Prompts, notes, voice and sound, and PDF or text knowledge as inputs on the canvas.

These nodes feed words, sound, and knowledge into the rest of your graph. They live in the **Text**, **Audio**, and **Document** sections of the **Add Node** menu.

## Text block

**Text Block** node: a prompt or enrichment input. Wire it into a generator's prompt.

**Inputs → outputs:** optional image, audio, document, or video → text.

## Note / annotation

**Note / Annotation** node: a free-text note on the canvas, for comments and instructions to your team. Press `⌘B` for bold. A note never runs and isn't part of the graph.

## Audio reference

The **Audio Reference** node brings in voice or sound.

**Inputs → outputs:** none → audio.

## Document context

The **Document Context** node adds PDF or text knowledge to a generation.

**Inputs → outputs:** none → document.

## Try it

Bring a product spec into a generation:

1. Add a **Document Context** node from the **Document** section, and load your product one-pager PDF.
2. Connect it to a **Text Block** that describes the shot, such as "hero shot of the bottle with the three key benefits".
3. Connect the Text Block to an **Image Generation** node's prompt, and choose **Run Node**.

Add a **Note / Annotation** beside the graph, such as "Use approved product shots only", so teammates know the rules.

Or ask Claude or ChatGPT:

* "On my open canvas, add a prompt that reads 'hero shot of the bottle with the three key benefits' and connect it to the image generator."
* "Add a note to my canvas that says 'Use approved product shots only'."

## What's next

* [Image nodes](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/canvas/nodes/image.md): Where most prompts go.
* [Node overview](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/canvas/nodes/overview.md): How nodes connect and run.

# Action and tool nodes

Source: https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/canvas/nodes/actions

> Deterministic edits to images, video, and text, plus Batch, Router, Export, and Continuity Frame.

The **Action** section of the **Add Node** menu holds two kinds of node. **Action** nodes apply one deterministic operation, with no generation and the same result every time. **Tools** shape how your graph runs and what comes out of it.

## Action

One operation, picked from the **Image ›**, **Video ›**, or **Text ›** menus.

### Image

| Group | Operations |
| - | - |
| **Colour** | Colour Grade, Filter, Tint, Blur, Shader Effect |
| **Transform** | Rotate, Flip, Chroma Key, Remove Background, Crop to Ratio, Pad to Ratio, Duplicate |
| **Overlay** | Burn In Text, Call To Action, Burn In Image |

### Video

Speed, Ken Burns, Stitch, Audio Bed, Split, Reverse, Boomerang, Long Exposure, Watermark, Greenscreen, Burn In, Subtitles, Editorial Captions, Extract Frames, and Frame Grid, among others.

### Text

Split Text, Find & Replace, and Join Text.

## Tools

| Node | What it does |
| - | - |
| **Batch** | A list of up to 100 inputs. Everything downstream runs once per item. Combine lists item by item (**zip**) or every item with every other (**cross**). |
| **Router** | Sends one output to several places without running it twice. |
| **Export** | Saves up to 20 media out as PNG, JPG, or WEBP; MP4, MOV, or GIF; or a ZIP of a batch. |
| **Continuity Frame** | Extracts the first, last, or an exact frame of a video as an image. |

## Try it

* **Make a square image vertical:** add **Action › Image › Pad to Ratio** after your generator, and pick `9:16`.
* **Hand off a batch:** add an **Export** node after a Batch run, and choose a ZIP.
* **From your assistant:** "On my open canvas, pad the hero image to 9:16 and run it."
* **From your assistant:** "Add a call-to-action overlay that says 'Shop the spring sale' to the finished image."

## What's next

* [Delivery nodes](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/canvas/nodes/delivery.md): Send finished creative to the Planner or a Meta ad.
* [Node overview](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/canvas/nodes/overview.md): How nodes connect and run.

# Delivery nodes

Source: https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/canvas/nodes/delivery

> Send finished creative from the canvas to an organic Planner draft, publish it to a platform, or replace the creative on a Meta ad.

Delivery nodes close the loop from canvas to channel. They live under **Action › Implementation** in the **Add Node** menu.

## Planner draft

The **Planner Draft** node finds or creates an organic draft in the [Calendar](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/organic/calendar.md), with its caption, schedule, and creative.

**Inputs → outputs:** a caption plus images or video → a Planner draft.

## Post to platform

The **Post to Platform** node posts a saved Planner draft. Connect a **Planner Draft** node to it, then choose:

* **Post now** — publish straight away.
* **Schedule for its planner time** — publish at the time set in the Calendar.

See [Publishing](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/organic/publishing.md) for where you can post.

**Inputs → outputs:** a Planner draft → a post.

## Paid ad

The **Paid Ad** node replaces the creative on a paused or active Meta ad.

**Inputs → outputs:** an image, carousel, or video → the ad's new creative.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Older canvases that used the **Video Splicer** or **Publish to Planner** nodes are converted automatically when they load: Video Splicer becomes a **Video Editor** node, and Publish to Planner becomes the publish node.

## Try it

Ask Claude or ChatGPT:

* "Put the finished image on next Tuesday's post."
* "Swap the winning image into our spring sale ad. Show me first."
* "Undo the creative swap on that ad."

Swapping a live ad's creative shows a preview and waits for your yes.

## What's next

* [Content calendar](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/organic/calendar.md): Where Planner drafts land.
* [Action and tool nodes](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/canvas/nodes/actions.md): Finish creative before you deliver it.

# Pipelines

Source: https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/canvas/pipelines

> Publish a canvas graph as a pipeline: a saved recipe with declared inputs that your team and your AI assistant can run with new material.

A **pipeline** is a saved canvas published with declared inputs and outputs — a recipe for a type of creative, such as a product lifestyle shot. Anyone on the brand with the **Operator** role or higher can run it with new material, without opening the graph. Running needs Operator because a run spends Canvas credits. Viewers can find a pipeline and see what it needs.

## Publish a pipeline

**1. Leave the inputs open**

Build the graph, and leave at least one required input unwired — a reference image or a prompt. Those open ports become the pipeline's inputs.

**2. Switch to Pipeline**

Right-click the canvas, choose **Save**, and switch the toggle to **Pipeline**. The dialog shows what it **Takes** as inputs.

**3. Describe it**

Fill in **What it makes and when to use it**.

**4. Write the agent guide**

Write or draft the **Agent guide** — when to use it and when to avoid it. Agents read it to decide when to run the pipeline.

**5. Publish**

Choose **Publish pipeline**.

## Run a pipeline

Open **Pipelines** in the [Library](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/canvas/library.md) sidebar, pick one, and choose **Set up run**. Provide the inputs — text, a Library asset, or an [Element](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/canvas/elements.md) — and choose **Run pipeline**. The run shows its outputs and cost when it finishes.

Published pipelines also appear in the **Pipelines** tab of **My Workflows** on the canvas.

## Try it

Ask Claude or ChatGPT:

* "Which pipelines do we have, and what does each one need?"
* "Run our customer-testimonial pipeline with these three angles: taste, price, convenience."
* "Run the product lifestyle pipeline five times with our hero product Element."
* "Is that pipeline run done yet?"

One request can make up to 10 versions. See [Make creative](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/mcp/use-cases/creative.md).

## What's next

* [Workflows](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/canvas/workflows.md): Save and load graphs.
* [Elements](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/canvas/elements.md): Keep subjects consistent across runs.

# Elements

Source: https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/canvas/elements

> Save a model, product, character, or style once and reuse it across every generation, so it looks the same everywhere.

An **Element** is a saved subject — a model, a product, a character, a style — that you reuse across generations so it looks the same in everything you make. Save it once, then wire it into any generation or mention it by name.

## What's in an Element

| Field | What it holds |
| - | - |
| **Name** | What you'll call it, and what you `@`-mention. |
| **Category** | What kind of subject it is (see below). |
| **Images** | Up to 8 images of the same subject. |
| **Guidelines** | How the subject should and shouldn't appear. |
| **Rights basis** | Why you're allowed to use the subject. |

Categories: **Model**, **Character**, **Product**, **Object**, **Material**, **Setting**, **Location**, **Landscape**, **Style**, **Moodboard**, **Palette**, **Animation**, **Effect**, and **General**.

## Create an Element

**1. Open Elements**

On the canvas, select **Elements** in the toolbar, or open **Elements** in the [Library](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/canvas/library.md) sidebar.

**2. Choose New Element**

Name it, pick a category, and add up to 8 images of the same subject.

**3. Add guidelines and rights**

Describe how the subject should appear, and record your rights basis.

## Use an Element

* **On the canvas:** add an [Element node](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/canvas/nodes/image.md) and connect it to a generation node as a reference.
* **In the Composer or a pipeline run:** type `@` and pick the Element.
* **From your AI assistant:** mention the Element by name in your request.

## Try it

Ask Claude or ChatGPT:

* "Which Elements do we have saved?"
* "Use our hero product Element for three new lifestyle images."
* "Run the product lifestyle pipeline with our spokesperson Element."

You create and edit Elements in the app. Your assistant can list and use them. See [Make creative](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/mcp/use-cases/creative.md).

## What's next

* [Image nodes](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/canvas/nodes/image.md): The Element node and the generators it feeds.
* [Pipelines](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/canvas/pipelines.md): Run a saved recipe with an Element as input.

# Video Studio

Source: https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/canvas/video-studio

> Edit video on a timeline: cut pauses, add captions, cut to the beat, reformat for each platform, and export to your Library.

**Video Studio** is Continuum's video editor. Turn raw footage into cuts for social — trim pauses, add captions and music, cut to the beat, and reformat for Reels, TikTok, or Shorts.

## Open Video Studio

* From the [Library](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/canvas/library.md): select a video and choose **Edit video** or **Edit in timeline**, or start a **New edit**.
* From the canvas: open a [Video Editor node](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/canvas/nodes/video.md).

## The workspace

| Area | Tabs |
| - | - |
| **Left panel** | **Media**, **Text**, **Graph**, **Generate** |
| **Right panel** | **Inspector**, **Agent** |

## Quick edits

| Edit | What it does |
| - | - |
| **Cut pauses** | Removes silences. |
| **Auto-captions** | Adds captions from the speech. |
| **Detect beats** | Finds the beats in the music. |
| **Cut on beat** | Cuts the edit to the beat. |

Music beds are available too. Generated voiceovers and music use Canvas credits; see [Providers and rates](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/providers-and-rates.md#voiceovers-and-music).

## Editing

The timeline supports **Split at playhead**, trimming the start or end to the playhead, **Ripple delete**, copy, paste, and duplicate, markers, and undo and redo. You can also:

* **First cut from a brief…** — describe the edit and get a first cut, with variants.
* **Ask the agent** — make changes in plain language.
* **Generate media** — create new footage or stills for the edit.

## Formats

Reformat for **TikTok**, **Instagram Reels**, **YouTube Shorts**, **YouTube**, **Feed 1:1**, or **Feed 4:5**.

## Export

Choose **Export…** to render an H.264 MP4. It's saved to your Library, with **Download MP4** and **Open in Library** when it's done.

## Try it

Ask Claude or ChatGPT:

* "Cut the pauses from my latest video and add captions."
* "Cut it to the beat of the music."
* "Reformat it for Reels and save it to the Library."
* "Undo that last change."

Every change shows up live in Video Studio, and every edit is saved as a version you can undo. See [Edit video](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/mcp/use-cases/video.md).

## What's next

* [Video nodes](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/canvas/nodes/video.md): Generate and extend footage on the canvas.
* [Library](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/canvas/library.md): Where exports land.

# Library

Source: https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/canvas/library

> Every image and video your brand has made, uploaded, or run as an ad, in one searchable place with versions, review status, comments, and share links.

The Library is your brand's media home. Every creative — generated, uploaded, or pulled from a campaign — lives here with its versions, review status, and comments, and you can share it with people outside your account.

## Media and Inspiration

The Library has two tabs:

* **Media** — your brand's own images and video.
* **Inspiration** — competitor organic posts and paid ad creatives to draw from. This is the same engine as [Brand Spy](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/brand/spy.md).

## Find your way around

The sidebar groups media so you can jump straight to it:

| Group | What's in it |
| - | - |
| **Home**, **Everything** | A starting view, and every asset. |
| **Images**, **Videos**, **Typography** | Media by type. |
| **Canvas** | Outputs from the [canvas](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/canvas/overview.md). |
| **Elements** | Your saved [Elements](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/canvas/elements.md). |
| **Source files**, **Templates** | Design files and templates. |
| **Needs review** | Work waiting on a decision. |
| **Pipelines** | Published [pipelines](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/canvas/pipelines.md), ready to run. |
| **Saved views**, **Collections**, **Trash** | Your own groupings, and deleted items. |

Switch between **grid**, **list**, **board**, and **reel** layouts.

## Where media comes from

Every asset carries its source, so you can filter by where it came from: **Uploads**, **AI Creations**, **Canvas**, **Inspiration**, **Ad Creatives**, **HyperFrames**, **Chat Uploads**, **Clips**, **Reels**, **Imported**, **Figma**, and **Forge renders**.

## Review and approve

Every asset has a review status: **None**, **Draft**, **In review**, **Needs changes**, or **Approved**. Your brand can rename these to match how your team works. Choose **Request review** to ask a teammate to look.

**Comments** can be pinned to a spot on an image or a moment in a video. They support `@`mentions and attachments, and you can lock a comment so it's internal only.

## Share outside your account

Create a **share link** to show work to a client or partner. Choose whether people can download, comment, or approve, and add a passcode and your logo.

## Use your media

* **Drag it onto the [canvas](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/canvas/overview.md)** as a reference.
* **Edit video** in [Video Studio](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/canvas/video-studio.md).
* **Run a pipeline** with an asset as input.
* **Put finished creative on a post** in the [content calendar](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/organic/calendar.md).

## Try it

Ask Claude or ChatGPT:

* "Find our approved product shots on a white background."
* "Which version of this ad creative is winning, and where is it running?"
* "Mark this image as needs changes, and leave a note about the logo placement."

Editing or deleting comments, collections, and share links stays in the app. See [Make creative](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/mcp/use-cases/creative.md).

## What's next

* [AI Canvas](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/canvas/overview.md): Make new creative from your media.
* [Brand Spy](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/brand/spy.md): Where competitor inspiration comes from.

# Forge

Source: https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/forge/overview

> Fill your design templates, including After Effects projects, with your messages, products, and offers to render many on-brand versions into your Library.

**Forge** fills your design templates — ready-made layouts, such as a promo video or a story card — to make many on-brand versions in one go. Fill a template's fields with your messages, products, and offers, preview every version, and render the set into your Library.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Forge is in **Creative+** in the sidebar and is part of the Performance+ plan. See [Billing](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/settings/billing.md).

## The three tabs

| Tab | What it's for |
| - | - |
| **Templates** | Your templates. Filter by **All**, **Ready**, **Drafts**, **Needs attention**, or **Shared with you**, and by animated or static. |
| **Render** | Fill a template's fields row by row, preview each version, and render. |
| **Render ledger** | Everything you've rendered. |

## Get a template set up

Templates are built from your team's design files. For an After Effects project, follow [After Effects delivery](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/forge/after-effects/overview.md) to structure it so every field you want to change is exposed cleanly, then hand it to your Continuum contact.

## Render versions

**1. Pick a template**

Open a template that's **Ready**, then go to **Render**.

**2. Fill the rows**

Each row is one version. Type the values in, or choose **Draft rows with AI** to write them from a brief.

**3. Preview**

Each row shows a live composed preview, so you see every version before anything is rendered.

**4. Render**

Final renders land in your Library under **Forge renders**.

## Render sets

Save a group of rows as a **render set** to come back to it. You can rename, duplicate, download, and share a set, see its version history, and update it to the template's current version.

## Try it

In the app, open a **Ready** template, go to **Render**, choose **Draft rows with AI**, and give it a brief such as "Six versions of our spring offer: three for price, three for free shipping."

Or ask Claude or ChatGPT:

* "Which templates do we have?"
* "Write six versions of the promo template from this brief."
* "Produce the whole set. Show me what will be made first."

From your assistant, you see a preview of every version, and nothing is made until you confirm. Filling a template needs the **Operator** role or higher, and final versions, rather than draft previews, need an **Admin** or **Owner**. See [Produce templates at scale](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/mcp/use-cases/templates.md).

For agent and application integration, use the [Forge agent quickstart](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/forge/agents.md),
[function reference](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/forge/functions.md), and [source-format map](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/forge/design-systems.md).
They separate file intake from editing and rendering, and explain how to retain template,
revision, set and job identities between calls.

## What's next

* [After Effects delivery](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/forge/after-effects/overview.md): Structure a project so Forge can render it.
* [Library](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/canvas/library.md): Where renders land.

# Use Forge from an agent

Source: https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/forge/agents

> Discover a template, map its fields, review a render and retrieve its outputs through the current Forge MCP contract.

Use Forge to fill an existing design with different messages, products or offers. Start here; load the [function reference](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/forge/functions.md) or a single action schema only when needed. Use the [operation index](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/forge/agent-manifest.json) for machine routing rather than loading the whole documentation site.

## Discover before calling

Connect through [MCP](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/quickstart.md#connect-your-assistant), call `brands_list`, select the intended brand with `brands_select`, and check `_brandContext` on results. Discover the selected action:

`{"name":"help_describe","arguments":{"tool":"forge_manage","action":"render_preview"}}`

These examples show MCP `tools/call` parameters. Replace illustrative IDs, tokens and keys with returned values. `help_describe` describes the server; it does not upgrade a client's cached tool schema. If your client cannot express an action, refresh discovery or use a compatible client. Never invent an alternative call.

## Fill and render a template

**1. Inspect**

Call `forge_query` with `action="templates"`. Select its `key` and `bindingId`; call `action="template"` with `templateKey` and that binding. Read variable keys, kinds, required fields, options, text budgets, outputs and `contractHash`. An empty template list is not a rendering failure.

**2. Map and save**

Map your event or brief into the returned variable keys. Media uses Library asset/version references, not guessed URLs. Call `forge_manage` with `action="set_create"`, `templateKey`, optional `bindingId`, a `name`, and `rows` containing `label`, `parentId` and `overrides`. A child row inherits its parent's values. Keep the returned set `id` and numeric `revision`.

For edits, read `forge_query action="set"` first. Use `rows_patch` with `expectedRevision` for selected changes; `set_update.rows` replaces every row. On a conflict, re-read and reconcile.

**3. Review**

Inspect the set's `resolved` rows and `settings`, then call `render_preview`. It validates readiness and returns destinations and `confirmationToken`; it does not render pixels. Omitted settings inherit, so check the saved Meta targets, Slack room and `final` setting. `slackDestinationId=null` disables posting. `final=true` needs Admin or Owner.

**4. Confirm**

Show rows and destinations; explain rendering can spend. Show a known estimate or say it is unavailable. Wait for the person's yes, then call `render_confirm` with the returned `confirmationToken`. Keep `batchId` and job IDs. A refusal stays blocking unless `details.overrides` names a flag and the person accepts that specific problem.

**5. Retrieve**

Use `forge_query action="batch"` with `batchId` and `waitSeconds=50` in a background task until `done=true`. Inspect each job's status and `outputs`; settled includes failed jobs. `action="job"` refreshes one render-set job. Preserve IDs and error reasons. After an uncertain confirmation response, inspect jobs before submitting again.

## Bring in or change a source

Use source preparation only where enabled for your brand and exposed by your client. Before uploading or saving an eligible source, obtain permission for automatic preparation and smoke-render spend: these can start without `template_forge`. `forge_manage source_begin` returns the upload `open_url`; read `source_status` with `upload_intent_id`, then `forge_query sources` for parse state and source `assetId`. Check [source families](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/forge/design-systems.md).

For a supported revision, read `template_tree`, `template_revision` and `template_layers`. Preview with `template_preview`; save with `template_save` using `parentRevisionId` and either a new `name` or the existing `variantId`. Keep the returned revision's `id` and `sourceAssetId`. The Original is preserved.

For eligible sources, inspect `template_run` using that exact `sourceAssetId`. Publishing can smoke-render and spend automatically: obtain permission first. Admin/Owner may use `template_forge` only when appropriate; re-read on conflicts and intervene only where the run parks. After publication, rediscover `templateKey` and `bindingId` through `sources`/`templates`. Pin the **published** revision UUID with `templateRevisionId` in `set_create` or `set_retarget`. Native HTML, components and Blender never enter `template_forge`.

## Render a scene

Read `forge_query scenes`. Pass its `assetId`, `versionId` and output IDs to `scene_fill`. Review returned values, outputs and potential spend; a price estimate may be unavailable. Recheck the scene before confirming; if it changed, fill/review again. `scene_render` reloads the current scene, so this is not an immutable-version guarantee. After the person's yes, pass its `confirmationToken`. Keep `jobs[].jobId`; use scene history in Forge and the Library for results, not render-set batches.

## Start from an external event

Your application turns an authorized event into the mapping above and retains brand, template/revision, set and job identifiers. Keep confirmation in that flow. No Forge webhook subscription or cancellation action is established here. Refresh short-lived output links when needed; a download URL is not a permanent resource identity.

## What's next

* [Function reference](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/forge/functions.md): Inputs, effects, permissions and retry behavior.
* [Design systems](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/forge/design-systems.md): Check each source's actual execution path.

# Forge function reference

Source: https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/forge/functions

> Choose a Forge MCP action, learn its prerequisites and follow its result without guessing identifiers or retry behavior.

{/* Generated by scripts/forge-docs.mjs; edit scripts/forge-notes.mjs instead. */}

Use [the quickstart](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/forge/agents.md) first. Every call uses the active brand and normal [MCP sign-in and access rules](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/mcp/reference.md).

Checked 2026-11-09: **17 query actions** and **19 management actions**. These are contract entries, not a promise that every source format or client can execute them.

Fetch only the action you need with `help_describe {tool, action}`. Some connectors advertise an older action enum. If your client cannot represent an action, refresh its tool discovery or use a client that exposes the current contract; do not silently substitute another action.

The [operation index](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/forge/agent-manifest.json) supplies compact routing facts. Full inputs stay in runtime discovery. Fields marked required below include action-specific validator requirements that a flat JSON schema may omit. Successful Forge results use `{status: "ok", action, result}`; read the fields below inside `result`.

> [!WARNING]
>
> `render_preview` is a preflight, not a pixel render. Inspect saved delivery settings: omitted settings inherit. Show the person the rows, destinations and any spend before confirming. Use the exact `confirmationToken` returned by the Forge action.

## At a glance

| Action | What it does | Role |
| - | - | - |
| [`forge_query.templates`](#forge_query-templates) | List granted or built render templates. | Viewer or higher |
| [`forge_query.template`](#forge_query-template) | Read exposed variables, required values, budgets, outputs and contractHash. | Viewer or higher |
| [`forge_query.sets`](#forge_query-sets) | List saved sets, optionally filtered by templateKey. | Viewer or higher |
| [`forge_query.set`](#forge_query-set) | Read saved rows, inherited effective values and delivery settings. | Viewer or higher |
| [`forge_query.set_revisions`](#forge_query-set_revisions) | Read kept states of a set. | Viewer or higher |
| [`forge_query.destinations`](#forge_query-destinations) | Read delivery and approval destinations. | Viewer or higher |
| [`forge_query.jobs`](#forge_query-jobs) | List render jobs, optionally filtered by templateKey, setId, batchId or status. | Viewer or higher |
| [`forge_query.job`](#forge_query-job) | Refresh a single render job and its output files. | Viewer or higher |
| [`forge_query.batch`](#forge_query-batch) | Read a batch, waiting briefly for its jobs to settle. | Viewer or higher |
| [`forge_query.scenes`](#forge_query-scenes) | List accessible 3D scenes and their fillable keys. | Viewer or higher |
| [`forge_query.set_diff`](#forge_query-set_diff) | Compare two rows or two kept states as rendered. | Viewer or higher |
| [`forge_query.template_tree`](#forge_query-template_tree) | Read branches, revision history, publications and the default variant. | Viewer or higher |
| [`forge_query.template_layers`](#forge_query-template_layers) | Read editable compositions and layers of a revision. | Viewer or higher |
| [`forge_query.template_revision`](#forge_query-template_revision) | Read a revision and its source identity. | Viewer or higher |
| [`forge_query.template_diff`](#forge_query-template_diff) | Compare edits of two revisions of one template. | Viewer or higher |
| [`forge_query.template_run`](#forge_query-template_run) | Read the publishing run for this exact revision source. | Viewer or higher |
| [`forge_query.sources`](#forge_query-sources) | List the brand’s uploaded template sources and parse/build state. | Viewer or higher |
| [`forge_manage.set_create`](#forge_manage-set_create) | Save rows for one template. | Operator or higher |
| [`forge_manage.set_update`](#forge_manage-set_update) | Update a saved set with a revision check. | Operator or higher |
| [`forge_manage.set_fork`](#forge_manage-set_fork) | Copy the current set or one of its kept states. | Operator or higher |
| [`forge_manage.set_delete`](#forge_manage-set_delete) | Delete a saved render set. | Operator or higher |
| [`forge_manage.suggest_rows`](#forge_manage-suggest_rows) | Draft values from a brief, documents or media. | Operator or higher |
| [`forge_manage.apply_suggestions`](#forge_manage-apply_suggestions) | Append selected draft rows once. | Operator or higher |
| [`forge_manage.source_begin`](#forge_manage-source_begin) | Create a signed-in mixed-file upload handoff. | Operator or higher |
| [`forge_manage.source_status`](#forge_manage-source_status) | Read upload readiness and classified resource IDs. | Operator or higher |
| [`forge_manage.source_figma`](#forge_manage-source_figma) | Import Figma frames as design templates, or list the frames in a Figma file. | Operator or higher |
| [`forge_manage.render_preview`](#forge_manage-render_preview) | Validate selected rows and show where each result will go. | Operator or higher |
| [`forge_manage.render_confirm`](#forge_manage-render_confirm) | Redeem the reviewed preflight token and queue the batch. | Operator or higher |
| [`forge_manage.scene_fill`](#forge_manage-scene_fill) | Fill an accessible scene from the brand and brief. | Operator or higher |
| [`forge_manage.scene_render`](#forge_manage-scene_render) | Redeem a reviewed scene fill and queue its outputs. | Operator or higher |
| [`forge_manage.rows_patch`](#forge_manage-rows_patch) | Upsert or remove selected rows with a revision check. | Operator or higher |
| [`forge_manage.set_retarget`](#forge_manage-set_retarget) | Pin an existing set to a published template revision. | Operator or higher |
| [`forge_manage.template_preview`](#forge_manage-template_preview) | Preview proposed edits without saving a revision. | Operator or higher |
| [`forge_manage.template_save`](#forge_manage-template_save) | Save edits as a new immutable revision. | Operator or higher |
| [`forge_manage.template_forge`](#forge_manage-template_forge) | Start or advance publication of an eligible revision source. | Admin or Owner |
| [`forge_manage.template_set_default`](#forge_manage-template_set_default) | Choose the variant everyone opens by default. | Admin or Owner |

## Sources

### `forge_query.sources`

List the brand’s uploaded template sources and parse/build state.

| Contract | Behavior |
| - | - |
| Required inputs | `action` |
| Conditions | Use only identifiers returned for this brand. |
| Returns | items: assetId, family, parseState, forgeState; more |
| Role | Viewer or higher |
| Side effects | Reads state; starts no render. |
| Potential spend | No generation started by this call. |
| Confirmation | None for this action. |
| Completion | Returns inline. |
| Retry | Safe to read again. |
| Errors | `needs_brand` / `needs_role`: resolve access first; `NOT_FOUND` / `VALIDATION_ERROR`: retain the returned reason |

Schema: `help_describe {"tool":"forge_query","action":"sources"}`.

### `forge_manage.source_begin`

Create a signed-in mixed-file upload handoff.

| Contract | Behavior |
| - | - |
| Required inputs | `action` |
| Conditions | Use only identifiers returned for this brand. |
| Returns | `upload_intent_id`, `open_url`, `expires_at`, `max_files` |
| Role | Operator or higher |
| Side effects | Creates an upload intent; completing an eligible source upload can start automatic preparation. |
| Potential spend | No generation started by this call. |
| Confirmation | Explain automatic preparation and smoke-render spend and obtain permission BEFORE completing an eligible source upload; waiting for `template_forge` does not prevent it. |
| Completion | Returns inline; upload, parsing and eligible preparation continue separately. |
| Retry | Do not retry blindly: another call creates another handoff. |
| Errors | `needs_brand` / `needs_role`: resolve access first; `NOT_FOUND` / `VALIDATION_ERROR`: retain the returned reason |

Schema: `help_describe {"tool":"forge_manage","action":"source_begin"}`.

### `forge_manage.source_status`

Read upload readiness and classified resource IDs.

| Contract | Behavior |
| - | - |
| Required inputs | `action`, `upload_intent_id` |
| Conditions | Use only identifiers returned for this brand. |
| Returns | documentIds, mediaAssetIds, templateAssetIds, `source_refs`, sources |
| Role | Operator or higher |
| Side effects | Reads the handoff; saves nothing. |
| Potential spend | No generation started by this call. |
| Confirmation | None for this action. |
| Completion | Returns inline. |
| Retry | Safe to read again while processing. |
| Errors | `needs_brand` / `needs_role`: resolve access first; `NOT_FOUND` / `VALIDATION_ERROR`: retain the returned reason |

### `forge_manage.source_figma`

| Contract | Behavior |
| - | - |
| Required inputs | `action`, `figmaUrl` |
| Conditions | Uses the brand's Figma connection and the signed-in person's Continuum session. Read `forge_query` sources until parsed, then `forge_query` template for its text columns. |

| Side effects | A file link lists its frames and imports nothing. A frame link, or figmaNodeIds (up to 5), imports each frame into the Library as a design template that renders as its templateKey with no build. |

| Confirmation | None for this action. |
| Completion | Returns inline. |
| Retry | If the call times out, repeat it with the same arguments: it joins the import still running. |
| Errors | `INTEGRATION_REQUIRED`: connect Figma for the brand; `PERMISSION_DENIED`: the brand's Figma account can't open this file; `NOT_FOUND`: no such Figma file or frame; UNAUTHENTICATED: no signed-in session; import from the Forge page instead; `VALIDATION_ERROR`: not a figma.com/design link |

Schema: `help_describe {"tool":"forge_manage","action":"source_figma"}`.

| Completion | Scene jobs use the template’s scene history in Forge and the Library; they are not Forge render-set batches. |
| Retry | Token is single-use; after an uncertain response inspect history before another fill/render. |
| Errors | `VALIDATION_ERROR`: `expired_confirmation`; CONFLICT: `confirmation_spent` |

Schema: `help_describe {"tool":"forge_manage","action":"scene_render"}`.

## Recover from a refusal

* **Revision conflict:** re-read the set or template head, reconcile the intended change, and preview again. A set's numeric `expectedRevision` is different from a template revision UUID.
* **Ambiguous template key:** select the discovered `bindingId`; do not guess a workspace.
* **Insufficient role:** preserve `needs_role` or `PERMISSION_DENIED` and request the appropriate brand role. `final=true` and template publication need Admin or Owner.
* **Expired or spent token:** inspect existing jobs first if submission may have succeeded. Otherwise preview/fill again and obtain a new yes; never turn an uncertain response into an automatic second render.
* **Missing fonts or another overridable refusal:** pass a flag only when `details.overrides` names it and the person explicitly accepts that specific problem. Other refusals remain blocking.
* **Partial or failed batch:** inspect each job. `done=true` means settled, including failures; it does not mean every output succeeded. Preserve job IDs and reasons.
* **Scene jobs:** use the template's scene history in Forge and the Library. Do not pass a scene job ID to the render-set job API without a supported contract.

No Forge webhook subscription or cancellation action is established by this catalog. Your host application starts MCP calls and retains their identifiers.

## Example call sequences

These are sequential MCP `tools/call` parameters, not an executable batch. UUIDs, tokens, template and variable keys are illustrative: substitute the exact discovered values. Populate required template fields before preflight. Obtain permission for automatic preparation/spend before completing a source upload or saving a revision; pause for the person's yes before render confirmation. A render price estimate may be unavailable.

Keep each returned identity for the next call. After publication, rediscover the matching template key/binding and use the published revision UUID. For scenes, recheck the version before confirming; the service still reloads the current scene. Follow the individual action's conditions above.

* **An existing template.** The discovered binding is 666…; `set_create` returns set id 555…; `render_confirm` returns batchId 777…. Replace each with its actual returned value. The illustrative headline key must also be replaced by an exposed variable key. Calls, in order: `[{"name":"forge_query","arguments":{"action":"template","templateKey":"discovered-template-key","bindingId":"66666666-6666-4666-8666-666666666666"}},{"name":"forge_manage","arguments":{"action":"set_create","templateKey":"discovered-template-key","name":"Example set","rows":[{"id":"22222222-2222-4222-8222-222222222222","parentId":null,"label":"Example","overrides":{"headline":"Your message"}}],"bindingId":"66666666-6666-4666-8666-666666666666"}},{"name":"forge_query","arguments":{"action":"set","setId":"55555555-5555-4555-8555-555555555555"}},{"name":"forge_manage","arguments":{"action":"render_preview","setId":"55555555-5555-4555-8555-555555555555","slackDestinationId":null,"final":false}},{"name":"forge_manage","arguments":{"action":"render_confirm","confirmationToken":"token-returned-by-render-preview"}},{"name":"forge_query","arguments":{"action":"batch","batchId":"77777777-7777-4777-8777-777777777777","waitSeconds":50}}]`
* **A supported source revision.** Upload intent: 888…. Uploaded source asset: 111…. Observed parent revision: 222…. `template_save` returns revision.sourceAssetId=333… and revision.id=444…. Use 333… for `template_run`/`template_forge`, and the published 444… for templateRevisionId. After publication, rediscover templateKey and bindingId (666…). The `template_forge` start example is CONDITIONAL: skip it if a run already exists. Wait for publication before `set_create`. Calls, in order: `[{"name":"forge_manage","arguments":{"action":"source_begin"}},{"name":"forge_manage","arguments":{"action":"source_status","upload_intent_id":"88888888-8888-4888-8888-888888888888"}},{"name":"forge_query","arguments":{"action":"sources"}},{"name":"forge_query","arguments":{"action":"template_tree","assetId":"11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111"}},{"name":"forge_query","arguments":{"action":"template_revision","revisionId":"22222222-2222-4222-8222-222222222222"}},{"name":"forge_query","arguments":{"action":"template_layers","revisionId":"22222222-2222-4222-8222-222222222222"}},{"name":"forge_manage","arguments":{"action":"template_preview","assetId":"11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111","parentRevisionId":"22222222-2222-4222-8222-222222222222","edits":{}}},{"name":"forge_manage","arguments":{"action":"template_save","assetId":"11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111","parentRevisionId":"22222222-2222-4222-8222-222222222222","edits":{},"name":"Example variant"}},{"name":"forge_query","arguments":{"action":"template_run","assetId":"33333333-3333-4333-8333-333333333333"}},{"name":"forge_manage","arguments":{"action":"template_forge","assetId":"33333333-3333-4333-8333-333333333333","step":"start","templateName":"example-template"}},{"name":"forge_manage","arguments":{"action":"set_create","templateKey":"discovered-template-key","name":"Example set","rows":[{"id":"22222222-2222-4222-8222-222222222222","parentId":null,"label":"Example","overrides":{"headline":"Your message"}}],"bindingId":"66666666-6666-4666-8666-666666666666","templateRevisionId":"44444444-4444-4444-8444-444444444444"}}]`
* **An accessible scene.** scenes supplies assetId 111… and versionId 222…. `scene_fill` returns the reviewed token; `scene_render` returns separate jobs\[].jobId values. Recheck the scene before confirmation; the current service does not enforce the token’s source version at render time. Calls, in order: `[{"name":"forge_query","arguments":{"action":"scenes"}},{"name":"forge_manage","arguments":{"action":"scene_fill","assetId":"11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111","versionId":"22222222-2222-4222-8222-222222222222","brief":{"headline":"Your message"}}},{"name":"forge_manage","arguments":{"action":"scene_render","confirmationToken":"token-returned-by-scene-fill"}}]`

# Forge design systems and source formats

Source: https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/forge/design-systems

> Separate brand grounding, accepted files and executable Forge workflows before choosing an agent function.

{/* Generated by scripts/forge-docs.mjs; edit scripts/forge-formats.mjs instead. */}

## Brand grounding and source support

Your brand kit supplies logos, palette and typography; the brand book supplies creative context. Those inputs do not add support for a source application, install a missing font, or make an unsupported feature editable. Inspect the exact template contract before mapping values.

**Upload → parse → edit → preview → render → export are separate capabilities.** Library acceptance, a thumbnail, a schema enum or a successful parse establishes only that stage. A preview may be a sidecar or a preflight rather than final pixels. No new customer rendering or fidelity qualification was performed for this map (checked 2026-11-09).

## Source families

| Source | Upload | Parse | Edit | Preview | Render | Export | Evidence boundary |
| - | - | - | - | - | - | - | - |
| After Effects | Project or collected package | Inspect parseState; missing dependencies can block | Exposed fields; supported revision layer/slot edits | Contract/revision preview and render preflight | Published template → render set | Files declared by the template outputs | Customer template rendering is documented; this mapping run starts no renders. |
| Photoshop / Illustrator | Accepted source files; EPS is Library intake | Source-specific import; inspect the actual result | Only the fields/layers the imported revision exposes | Library preview or supported template preview | Only after a usable template is published | Declared output files; no promise of PSD/AI round-trip | Upload is documented. Arbitrary-file fidelity and end-to-end rendering are not established by this map. |
| Presentations | Library intake | Inspect the source parse result | No presentation-specific action in the captured Forge surface | Companion preview when available | No general deck-render action documented here | Original download; do not infer PPTX/PDF generation | Library support does not establish an agent authoring/export workflow. |
| Premiere Pro | Library project storage | Not a template family in the captured source contract | No Forge project-edit action verified | Sidecar video, when supplied | No Forge project-render action verified | Original project download | A project file and a rendered movie are different resources. |
| HTML / HyperFrames | HTML or classified bundle | Native source; inspect family and parseState | Only the native contract’s exposed fields | Source/Library preview does not certify rendered frames | Use only the execution path exposed for that source | Only artifacts returned by that path | Does not enter `template_forge`. Browser/native rendering fidelity is not qualified by this documentation run. |
| Web components | ZIP with a recognized component manifest | Bundle contents decide the family | Declared component contract only | Inspect the source’s supported preview | Only an exposed template/output contract | Returned artifacts, not arbitrary source conversion | Does not enter `template_forge`. A generic ZIP is not automatically a component. |
| Blender / scenes | Library source; accessible scenes come from scenes | Inspect native source/scene readiness | `scene_fill` values, not unrestricted scene editing | Review filled values; this is not a pixel preview | `scene_fill` → `scene_render` for listed outputs | Scene results in Library; use scene history | Does not enter `template_forge`. No arbitrary customer-scene fidelity claim. |
| Figma | `forge_manage` `source_figma` with a frame or file link (up to 5 frames) | Each frame becomes a web-component template; read `forge_query` sources until parsed | The text columns `forge_query` template exposes | `render_preview` preflight for its render set | Renders as its templateKey (web: plus the asset id) with no build | Returned render outputs; no Figma round-trip | Needs the brand's Figma connection. A file link only lists frames. |
| Canva | Not a local-file extension promise | Connected import is separate from file intake | No dedicated action in the captured Forge pair | Do not infer from connection availability | No general execution recipe verified here | No round-trip promise | A connection or source-family enum alone is not an executable function. |
| CAD / 3D model files | Library model intake; CAD has separate tools | Use the CAD capability guide for CAD resources | Not `forge_manage` template edits | Model viewer does not establish CAD rendering | Separate `cad_query` / `cad_manage` contract | Separate CAD artifacts; no manufacturing qualification implied | Adjacent interface, not a Forge render-set family. Inspect `help_describe` before use. |
| Fonts | Licensed font intake | Font metadata and dependency checks | A dependency, not an image/template | No standalone font preview promise | Required faces can block template rendering | Do not assume fonts can be downloaded or redistributed | Brand typography names do not prove the required font bytes are available. |
| Other design files | Library intake | No blanket Forge parser guarantee | No blanket template-edit guarantee | Raster/embedded/companion strategy varies by format | Only if an executable template is separately discovered | Original download; no conversion promise | Library preview strategies are not Forge renderer qualification. |
| Media, documents and other files | Library or mixed-file handoff | Document/media classification is not template parsing | Use the relevant Library/Canvas/video tool | Depends on media format and proxy availability | No template engine implied by storage | Original or explicitly returned artifacts | Store source identity and version IDs; refresh short-lived signed URLs as needed. |

## Route by returned identity

* **Published render template:** discover `templateKey`, `bindingId` where needed, variable keys and outputs. Use sets and the render-preview/confirm sequence.
* **Revision source:** keep `assetId`, `variantId` and `revisionId` distinct. Inspect its layers; save immutable revisions rather than replacing the Original. Publication requires an eligible source and appropriate role.
* **Native HTML, component or Blender source:** follow its own exposed contract. Never send it into `template_forge` just because it parsed.
* **Scene:** use the `assetId`, exact `versionId` and output IDs returned by `scenes`, then `scene_fill` and `scene_render`.
* **CAD or another adjacent tool:** load that tool's current guide. Forge identifiers, editing rules and status readers do not transfer automatically.

A ZIP's contents decide its family. A stored original is not proof that an editable export or another application's native project can be generated. Ask for only the outputs the discovered contract declares.

## Before a render

Check fonts, field kinds, required values, text budgets, media/version references, output IDs and the saved delivery settings. Preserve any refusal. Brand-book grounding cannot override a missing dependency or renderer limitation.

## What's next

* [Agent quickstart](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/forge/agents.md): Choose a function and execute safely.
* [Function reference](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/forge/functions.md): Inspect the selected action.

# After Effects delivery

Source: https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/forge/after-effects/overview

> How to prepare and hand off an After Effects project so Continuum can turn it into scalable render variations.

Continuum can turn a single After Effects project into many on-brand render variations — swapping prices, product images, and copy without rebuilding the design each time. This section explains how to structure and deliver your project so integration is fast and clean.

## How integration works

You build the After Effects project to the requirements in this guide, then hand it off as a single packaged file. Continuum's engineering team integrates it into the render pipeline, wiring each **dynamic asset** you exposed into a swappable field. From there, one project produces many renders — each with different prices, images, or text — with no additional design work.

This is a collaborative handoff. You own the design and how it's structured; Continuum owns the integration and rendering. The more cleanly your project meets the requirements here, the faster it goes live.

Once it's live, the project is a template in [Forge](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/forge/overview.md), where you fill its fields and render versions.

## Dynamic vs. static assets

Every layer in your project is one of two things:

* **Dynamic** — anything that changes between renders: a price, a product image, a headline, or a paragraph of body copy. Dynamic assets must be built so Continuum can swap them.
* **Static** — the design that stays the same across every render: backgrounds, decorative elements, fixed brand marks.

Getting this split right is the most important part of preparation. If an asset should vary between renders, it must be dynamic — layered, exposed, and preset per the next page.

## Key terms

| Term | What it means |
| - | - |
| **Dynamic asset** | A layer whose content changes between renders (price, image, headline, body copy). |
| **Composition** | An After Effects comp. A single project file can contain several. |
| **Essential Graphics** | The After Effects panel where you expose dynamic assets so they can be controlled outside the timeline. |
| **Render** | One output variation produced from your project with a specific set of dynamic values. |
| **Animation preset** | A Continuum-provided preset applied to a dynamic asset so it fits the design at any size. |
| **Package** | The self-contained project folder produced by **File → Dependencies → Collect Files** for handoff. |

## Try it

Sort your layers before you build anything else:

1. In After Effects, list every layer in your main comp and mark each one dynamic or static. For example, "Price — dynamic", "Hero product image — dynamic", "Background gradient — static".
2. For each dynamic layer, follow [Preparing your project](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/forge/after-effects/preparing.md).
3. Package the project with **File → Dependencies → Collect Files** and hand the folder to your Continuum contact.

Once your template is live in Forge, ask Claude or ChatGPT:

* "Which templates do we have?"
* "Write six versions of the promo template from this brief."

## What's next

* [Preparing your project](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/forge/after-effects/preparing.md): Structure layers, expose dynamic assets, and apply presets.
* [Delivery & handoff](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/forge/after-effects/delivery.md): Provide fonts, wire up asset access, and package the project.

# Preparing your project

Source: https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/forge/after-effects/preparing

> Structure your After Effects project so every dynamic asset can be swapped without rework.

Follow these steps as you build your After Effects project. Each one makes a specific asset controllable at render time — skip one and that asset can't be swapped without going back into After Effects.

**1. Layer every dynamic asset separately**

Give each dynamic asset its own layer. Anything that should change between renders — a price, a product image, a headline — must be isolated so it can be targeted on its own.

Do not flatten, merge, or pre-compose dynamic assets together. If two prices share a layer, neither can be swapped independently.

**2. Expose dynamic assets in Essential Graphics**

Add every dynamic layer to the **Essential Graphics** panel. This is what lets Continuum control the asset without opening the timeline.

Expose each asset **relative to the composition it belongs to**. When a single project file contains multiple compositions, an asset must be added to the Essential Graphics panel for its own composition — not a different one.

> [!NOTE]
>
> The per-composition scoping only matters when your project file contains more than one composition. With a single composition, add every dynamic asset to that composition's panel.

**3. Make prices live text layers**

Build prices as **text layers**, sitting on top of the design that backs them — never baked into an image.

A live text layer means one design supports unlimited price variations with zero additional assets. Continuum simply changes the text for each render.

> [!TIP]
>
> The same rule applies to any dynamic copy — headlines, offers, disclaimers. Keep it as editable text, not flattened artwork.

**4. Design for the longest variation**

Leave room for the longest possible value a dynamic asset can hold. A price layered on a price-tag design needs enough space for the widest price you might ever render — not just the one on screen while you design.

Your design language has to hold up as text grows and shrinks. If the layout only works for `$9`, it will break on `$1,299.99`.

**5. Apply Continuum animation presets**

Continuum provides animation presets that keep dynamic assets fitting the design as their content changes. Apply a preset to **every** dynamic asset before delivery.

| Dynamic asset type | Preset required |
| - | - |
| Images | Yes |
| Single-line text | Yes |
| Paragraph text (2+ lines) | Yes |

> [!NOTE]
>
> Ask your Continuum contact for the current preset pack before you start applying them.

## Try it

Make a price swappable and test it at its longest:

1. Rename the price text layer to something clear, such as "Price — headline offer".
2. Open **Window → Essential Graphics**, set **Primary** to the price's own composition, and drag the layer's **Source Text** property into the panel.
3. Type the longest value you might ever render, such as "\$1,299.99", into the layer and check the layout still holds. Then set it back.
4. Apply the Continuum animation preset to the layer.

Repeat for each dynamic image and line of copy before you move on to [Delivery & handoff](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/forge/after-effects/delivery.md).

## What's next

* [Delivery & handoff](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/forge/after-effects/delivery.md): Provide fonts, wire up asset access, and package the project for handoff.

# Delivery & handoff

Source: https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/forge/after-effects/delivery

> Provide fonts, wire up asset access, package the project, and hand it off.

Once your project is built to spec, deliver it so Continuum has everything needed to render — fonts, asset access, and a complete package.

## Provide your fonts

Include the actual font files your design uses — `.otf` or `.ttf`. Continuum needs the files themselves so text renders exactly as you designed it; a font name alone is not enough.

Every typeface used by any text layer must be provided. Missing fonts cause substituted type and broken layouts at render time.

## Asset access

If you're a large domain with a big catalog — many products, prices, or images — provide **API access** so Continuum can gather assets and values programmatically. This scales far better than delivering assets one by one, and keeps renders in sync as your catalog changes.

For a small, fixed set of assets, delivering the files directly in your package is fine.

## Package the project

Export your project through **File → Dependencies → Collect Files** in After Effects. This bundles the project file, every piece of footage it depends on, and your fonts into a single self-contained folder.

> [!WARNING]
>
> Delivery is not complete without a **Collect Files** package. A bare `.aep` leaves out the footage and fonts it depends on, and the project cannot be integrated.

Hand off the resulting folder to your Continuum contact.

## Pre-delivery checklist

Run through this before you send:

| Check | Requirement |
| - | - |
| Layers | Every dynamic asset is on its own separate layer. |
| Essential Graphics | Every dynamic asset is exposed, scoped to its own composition. |
| Prices | Prices are live text layers on top of their backing design. |
| Space | Layouts hold the longest possible value for each dynamic asset. |
| Presets | Continuum animation presets are applied to every dynamic asset. |
| Fonts | All font files (`.otf` / `.ttf`) are included. |
| Asset access | API access is provided if you're a large domain. |
| Package | The project is exported via **File → Dependencies → Collect Files**. |

## Try it

1. In After Effects, choose **File → Dependencies → Collect Files**, and choose to collect all files.
2. Name the folder after the project, such as `SpringPromo_9x16_handoff`, and open it. Check that every font your text layers use is there, such as `BrandSans-Bold.otf`. Add any font file that's missing.
3. Run through the checklist above, then send the folder to your Continuum contact.

Once the template is published, ask your assistant:

* "Which Forge templates are published and ready to render?"
* "Make a render set from the spring promo template with these three headlines."
* "Preview the render for that set, and show me where each version will go before anything is queued."

## What's next

* [Back to overview](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/forge/after-effects/overview.md): Review how integration works and the key terms.

# Brand Spy

Source: https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/brand/spy

> Track competitors' organic posts and paid ad creatives in one workspace.

Brand Spy is your competitor intelligence workspace. It tracks the brands you compete with — their organic Instagram posts and their paid ad creatives — so you can see what they're running and pull ideas into your own work.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Brand Spy is in the **Creative+** section of the sidebar.

## The four tabs

| Tab | What it shows |
| - | - |
| **Inspiration** | A browser of competitor organic posts and paid ad creatives; save anything to a board. |
| **Report** | An awareness report on how you stack up against tracked competitors. |
| **Boards** | Your saved inspiration boards. |
| **Competitors** | The competitors you track, each with a health signal, plus recommended ones to add. |

## Tracking competitors

**1. Add competitors**

Search for a competitor and add them to your tracked list. Continuum also recommends competitors based on your onboarding.

**2. Browse their creative**

In **Inspiration**, switch between organic posts and paid ad creatives, and filter by competitor.

**3. Save to a board**

Save the creatives worth referencing to a board so your team can find them later.

> [!TIP]
>
> Tracking a competitor's organic posts uses Instagram data — connect an Instagram account in [Integrations](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/integrations.md) to get the most out of Brand Spy.

## Try it

* "Which competitor ads have been running the longest? What does that tell us?"
* "What have our competitors posted on Instagram this month?"
* "Where are competitors winning that we aren't even showing up?"
* "Run a fresh competitor scan."
