# Organic+

Source: https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/organic/overview

> Plan from the trends, draft with the Organic agent, publish from the calendar, and learn from what performed.

Organic+ is your workspace for organic social. It plans and writes your calendar from your brand book and your own account performance — captions, formats, carousels, reels — and you edit anything before it goes out.

* [Organic agent](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/organic/agent.md): Your social strategist: ideas, captions, and content plans.
* [Content calendar](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/organic/calendar.md): Plan from trends, events, and audience questions.
* [Publishing](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/organic/publishing.md): Approve a post and Continuum publishes it.
* [Organic analytics](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/organic/analytics.md): See how posted content performed.

> [!NOTE]
>
> In the sidebar, Organic+ shows **Organic Agent**, **Organic Analytics**, and **Calendar**. Inside the workspace, the calendar is the **Planner** tab and analytics is **Metrics**.

## How it fits together

**1. Find the angle**

Trends, key events, and audience questions in your niche seed ideas. The [Organic agent](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/organic/agent.md) turns them into a plan.

**2. Plan and draft**

Drafts land in the [calendar](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/organic/calendar.md), where you edit captions, formats, and creative. Creative from the [AI Canvas](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/canvas/overview.md) can go straight onto a draft with a [Planner Draft node](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/canvas/nodes/delivery.md).

**3. Approve and publish**

Approve and schedule a post, and Continuum [publishes](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/organic/publishing.md) it.

**4. Learn**

[Organic analytics](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/organic/analytics.md) shows what worked, and the agent uses it when it plans the next round.

## Try it

Ask Claude or ChatGPT:

* "Plan next week's Instagram content around our autumn launch."
* "What's ready to post right now?"
* "Ask the Organic agent which content themes we should lean into next month."

You can also rewrite captions, move posts, and publish to Instagram from your assistant. See [Plan and publish social content](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/mcp/use-cases/social.md).

## What's next

* [Start with the agent](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/organic/agent.md): Ask it to plan your next posts.
* [Open the calendar](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/organic/calendar.md): Turn insights into drafts.

# Organic agent

Source: https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/organic/agent

> An AI agent that plans posts, drafts concepts, and hands work into your content calendar.

The Organic agent is a conversational partner for organic social. You describe what you want and it plans, drafts, and organizes content — grounded in your [brand book](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/brand/overview.md) — then hands the results into your [content calendar](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/organic/calendar.md).

## What it can do

* **Plan posts** — propose a content plan for a theme, platform, or timeframe.
* **Draft concepts** — turn an idea into a concrete post concept you can refine.
* **Generate in bulk** — produce a batch of planned posts in one run.
* **Suggest creative skills** — recommend [creative skills](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/canvas/skills-and-grounding.md) to shape the look and voice.
* **Search your media** — pull relevant assets from your [Library](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/canvas/library.md).
* **Hand off to the calendar** — send plans and concepts into the calendar as drafts.

## Working with the agent

Ask in plain language. The agent replies with structured cards you can accept, edit, or send to the calendar. Because it draws on your brand book, drafts come back on-brand by default.

## Try it

In the Organic agent, ask:

* "Plan a week of reels about our summer launch."
* "Draft three carousel concepts for our new oat-milk latte."
* "Suggest creative skills for a calmer, more premium look."

From Claude or ChatGPT, ask: "Ask the Organic agent for five caption ideas for Friday's reel."

## What's next

* [Content calendar](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/organic/calendar.md): Where the agent's plans become scheduled drafts.
* [Organic analytics](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/organic/analytics.md): Measure what you publish.

# Content calendar

Source: https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/organic/calendar

> Plan organic content in the Planner: seed it from trends and signals, add posts, carousels, and reels, and approve and schedule them.

The content calendar — the **Planner** — is where organic content gets planned and scheduled. It starts from brand-relevant signals and turns them into **drafts** you refine, approve, and schedule across platforms.

## Choose a view

Switch between **Week**, **Month**, and **List** to plan at the cadence you want.

## Seed it with trends and signals

Open the **Trends & Signals** drawer and choose **Generate Trends** to pull what's relevant to your niche right now. Filter by:

* **Events** — seasonal and calendar moments worth posting around.
* **Questions** — what your audience is actually asking.
* **Rising momentum** — trends that are picking up.

Pick the ones worth acting on and turn them into drafts.

## Add posts

| Option | What you get |
| - | - |
| **New post** | A single-image or video post. |
| **New carousel** | A multi-slide post. |
| **New reel** | A short vertical video. |
| **AI one-shot post** | Describe the post and the AI writes and makes it for the day and platform you picked. |

The [Organic agent](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/organic/agent.md) can also fill the calendar with a plan in one go.

## Draft statuses

The main path a post takes:

A post's main path: 1. Concept. 2. Generating. 3. Draft. 4. Scheduled. 5. Published.

| Status | What it means |
| - | - |
| `Concept` | A planned idea. Nothing has been generated yet. |
| `Seeded` | A slot is created and waiting for generation. |
| `Queued` | Waiting for a generation slot. |
| `Generating` | Being generated right now. |
| `Draft` | Written, and not yet approved for posting. |
| `Scheduled` | Approved. It will post at the scheduled time. |
| `Published` | Live on the platform. |
| `Media failed` | The copy is saved, but the media didn't render. |
| `Failed` | Generation or publishing didn't complete. See [Publishing](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/organic/publishing.md). |
| `Cancelled` | Stopped before it finished. |

## Approve and schedule

Edit each draft — caption, format, creative, and slot — then choose **Approve & schedule**. The draft moves to `Scheduled` and posts at its scheduled time.

> [!TIP]
>
> Made something on the canvas? A [Planner Draft node](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/canvas/nodes/delivery.md) puts it straight onto a draft, and a canvas workspace opened from the Planner has **Apply Back to Planner**.

## Try it

In the Planner, open **Trends & Signals**, choose **Generate Trends**, and filter by **Events** to find a seasonal moment worth a post.

Or ask Claude or ChatGPT:

* "Plan next week's Instagram content around our autumn launch."
* "What's trending in our category this week, and what could we post about it?"
* "Move all of Thursday's posts to Friday."
* "Approve next week's plan. Show me first."

## What's next

* [Publishing](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/organic/publishing.md): Where posts go and what each status means.
* [Organic agent](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/organic/agent.md): Let the agent fill your calendar.

# Publishing

Source: https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/organic/publishing

> Which platforms Continuum publishes to, how to post an approved draft now or on schedule, and what to do when a post fails.

Publishing runs from inside Continuum: you approve a post in the Planner and Continuum publishes it. It's approval-first by design — nothing goes out until a person approves it.

## Where you can publish

| Platform | Status |
| - | - |
| **Instagram** | Live and in use. |
| **Facebook**, **LinkedIn**, **TikTok**, **YouTube** | [Contact support](mailto:support@trycontinuum.ai) before your first post on each, and the Continuum team publishes it with you. |

> [!NOTE]
>
> TikTok posts publish as private, visible only to the account, until TikTok's app audit completes.

You can plan and track posts for every platform in the [calendar](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/organic/calendar.md), whether or not it publishes from Continuum yet.

## Publish a post

**1. Finish the draft**

Edit the caption, format, creative, and slot in the [Planner](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/organic/calendar.md).

**2. Approve and schedule**

Choose **Approve & schedule**. The post's status changes to `Scheduled`.

**3. Check the result**

When it goes out, the status changes to `Published`. If it didn't, it shows `Failed`.

From the canvas, a [Post to Platform node](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/canvas/nodes/delivery.md) can **Post now** or **Schedule for its planner time**.

## If a post fails

* Check the connection is healthy under **Settings → Integrations**. A lapsed connection shows a **Re-sync** action. See [Integrations](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/integrations.md).
* `Media failed` means the copy is saved but the media didn't render. Regenerate or replace the media.

## Try it

Ask Claude or ChatGPT:

* "Show me Tuesday's approved carousel as it will post, then publish it."
* "Which posts failed to publish this week?"
* "Is our Instagram connection healthy?"

Your assistant always shows the post as it will go out and waits for your yes. Publishing from your assistant is available for Instagram today. See [Plan and publish social content](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/mcp/use-cases/social.md).

## What's next

* [Content calendar](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/organic/calendar.md): Plan and approve posts.
* [Organic analytics](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/organic/analytics.md): See how published posts performed.

# Organic analytics

Source: https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/organic/analytics

> Track organic performance across platforms and see where your audience is.

Organic analytics shows how your posted content performs across every connected platform, so you can see what's working and feed it back into planning.

## What you'll see

* **Per-platform performance** — organic results across Instagram, Facebook, TikTok, YouTube, and LinkedIn, side by side.
* **Audience location** — where your audience is, shown on a map.
* **Content performance** — how individual posts are doing over time.

Data appears for each platform you've connected and assigned to this brand. See [Integrations](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/integrations.md) to connect more.

## Closing the loop

Use what you learn here to steer the next round: hand the [Organic agent](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/organic/agent.md) your best-performing themes, and build more drafts around them in the [calendar](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/organic/calendar.md).

## Try it

Ask Claude or ChatGPT:

* "What were our three best Instagram posts last month, and why did they work?"
* "Which TikTok posts had the highest engagement rate in the last 30 days?"
* "Where are our Instagram followers based, and what's the age mix?"

## What's next

* [Content calendar](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/organic/calendar.md): Act on what's working.
* [Paid analytics](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/performance/analytics.md): See the paid side of performance.

# Performance+

Source: https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/performance/overview

> Run paid media in one place, where the Optimizer proposes budget moves, Jaina explains the numbers, and you approve.

Performance+ is where you run paid media. It brings your ad accounts, performance, and optimization into one place.

How a budget move happens: 1. The Optimizer proposes. 2. Jaina explains. 3. You approve (your step). 4. The move is applied.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Performance+ is part of the Performance+ plan. See [Billing](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/settings/billing.md) and [pricing](https://trycontinuum.ai/#pricing).

## The three tabs

In the sidebar, Performance+ shows **Jaina**, **Paid Analytics**, and **Paid Optimization**. Inside the workspace they're the **Jaina**, **Dashboard**, and **Optimization** tabs.

* [Paid analytics](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/performance/analytics.md): Campaign and ad-set performance with budget pacing.
* [Paid optimization](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/performance/optimizer.md): Review and apply budget recommendations.
* [Jaina](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/performance/jaina.md): Ask the ads analyst why results changed.

[Approvals](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/performance/approvals.md) lists what waits for a person in Performance+, and who can give the yes.

## What's supported

| Platform | In Performance+ |
| - | - |
| **Meta** | Performance, creative, budgets, and reporting, with optimization and campaign management on the same connection. |
| **LinkedIn** | Paid performance is visible. Managing LinkedIn ads stays in LinkedIn for now. |

New campaigns, ad sets, and ads Continuum creates are always **paused** until an Admin or Owner approves switching them on.

## Try it

Everything here is also reachable from Claude or ChatGPT. Ask:

* "Ask Jaina why our cost per purchase jumped last week."
* "Show me this week's budget recommendations and explain each one."
* "Set up a paused campaign to drive traffic to our spring sale."

See [Run your Meta ads](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/mcp/use-cases/ads.md).

## What's next

* [Connect an ad account](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/integrations.md): Link Meta to populate Performance+.
* [Ask Jaina](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/performance/jaina.md): Get a read on what's working.

# Jaina

Source: https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/performance/jaina

> The paid-media analyst — ask about performance and get a structured report with prioritized recommendations.

Jaina is your paid-media analyst. Ask a question in plain language — "why did ROAS drop last week?" — and Jaina analyzes your connected accounts and returns a structured **checkpoint report** rather than a wall of text.

## What a report contains

* **KPI metrics** — the numbers that matter for your question, laid out as a grid.
* **Charts** — visual trends behind the numbers.
* **Strategic insights** — what the data means.
* **Prioritized recommendations** — concrete next steps, each tagged with **impact** and **effort** so you know what to do first.

## Where to use Jaina

* As the **Jaina** tab in [Performance+](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/performance/overview.md), with a side canvas and full-screen mode for deeper sessions.
* From Claude or ChatGPT, through the connector. See [Understand your performance](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/mcp/use-cases/performance.md).

## When Jaina proposes a move

Jaina can also propose the next move — a new audience, a set of creative angles, a creative slate, a pipeline run, or an Optimizer approval. Nothing touches your ad account or spends anything until you approve that exact action in the chat.

> [!TIP]
>
> Jaina reads the ad accounts assigned to your active brand. Connect and assign accounts in [Integrations](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/integrations.md) first.

## Try it

In the **Jaina** tab, ask the question directly: "Why did ROAS drop last week?"

From Claude or ChatGPT, ask:

* "Ask Jaina why our cost per purchase jumped last week."
* "Ask Jaina where to cut \$2,000 from next week's Meta spend."
* "Ask Jaina for a weekly report on our Meta ads, with the top three actions."

Asking Jaina from your assistant needs the **Operator** role or higher.

## What's next

* [Paid analytics](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/performance/analytics.md): The dashboards Jaina reasons over.
* [Paid optimization](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/performance/optimizer.md): Turn recommendations into applied actions.

# Paid optimization

Source: https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/performance/optimizer

> The Optimizer watches ad-set performance daily and proposes budget moves, with the reasoning attached, for you to approve.

Paid optimization — the Optimizer — watches ad-set performance daily and proposes budget moves with the reasoning attached. You approve them. It works across **portfolios** of ad sets rather than one campaign at a time.

> [!NOTE]
>
> The sidebar labels this **Paid Optimization**. Inside Performance+ it's the **Optimization** tab.

## How it's organized

| Tab | What it shows |
| - | - |
| **Overview** | The state of optimization across your portfolios at a glance. |
| **Portfolios** | Your portfolios, their ad sets, and their pending recommendations. |
| **Actions** | Recommendations to review, approve, or reject. |
| **Activity** | A history of what's been actioned. |

## Modes

Each portfolio runs in one of three modes:

| Mode | What happens |
| - | - |
| **Observe** | The Optimizer watches and reports. |
| **Recommend** | It proposes budget moves for you to approve or reject. |
| **Autopilot** | It applies moves automatically, inside caps you set. |

Autopilot is opt-in for each portfolio. You can arm it only once both guardrail caps are set — a maximum daily spend change and a maximum change per cycle. It never pauses anything without you approving that specific pause.

> [!TIP]
>
> Start in **Recommend** and run the first few cycles yourself. Turn on Autopilot from the dashboard; your assistant can't switch a portfolio to it.

## Working with recommendations

Review each recommendation and its reasoning under **Actions**, then approve or reject it. Everything that's been done appears under **Activity**. If a portfolio isn't set up or an account is offline, the Optimizer tells you what to connect first.

## Try it

Ask Claude or ChatGPT:

* "Show me this week's budget recommendations and explain each one."
* "Why does the Optimizer want to move budget off our retargeting ad set?"
* "Approve the recommendations for our prospecting campaigns, and reject the rest."

Approving a recommendation applies it right away. Your approval is the yes. Approving or rejecting needs the **Operator** role or higher; Viewers can read recommendations and their reasoning.

## What's next

* [Ask Jaina](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/performance/jaina.md): Get the reasoning behind a recommendation.
* [Run your Meta ads from your assistant](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/mcp/use-cases/ads.md): Approve recommendations in Claude or ChatGPT.

# Paid analytics

Source: https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/performance/analytics

> Campaign and ad-set performance across your ad accounts, with budget pacing and a feed of pending actions.

Paid analytics is your dashboard for everything running. It brings your connected ad accounts into one workspace so you can see performance, pacing, and where to act.

> [!NOTE]
>
> The sidebar labels this **Paid Analytics**; inside Performance+ it's the **Dashboard** tab.

## What's on the dashboard

* **Campaign and ad-set workspace** — performance across the ad accounts assigned to this brand.
* **Budget pacing** — how spend is tracking against plan, so you catch over- and under-pacing early.
* **Insight panels** — account- and campaign-level breakdowns of what's driving results.

Data appears for each ad account you've connected and assigned. See [Integrations](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/integrations.md) to add more.

## From insight to action

When you want to go deeper, ask [Jaina](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/performance/jaina.md) about anything on the dashboard, or move to [Paid optimization](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/performance/optimizer.md) to apply recommendations.

## Try it

Ask Claude or ChatGPT:

* "Which Meta campaigns are spending slower than planned this month?"
* "Show our top five Meta ads by ROAS over the last 30 days."
* "Break down the last two weeks of Meta spend by age and gender. Where are we wasting money?"

## What's next

* [Paid optimization](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/performance/optimizer.md): Act on the numbers.
* [Jaina](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/performance/jaina.md): Ask why the numbers moved.

# Approvals

Source: https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/performance/approvals

> What waits for a person's yes in Performance+, who can give it, and where: budget recommendations, Jaina's proposals, ad changes, and switching ads on.

Changes to your ad account wait for a person to approve that exact change. "The Optimizer proposes. Jaina explains. You approve." The one exception is [Autopilot](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/performance/optimizer.md#modes), which you turn on for a portfolio and which applies budget moves inside caps you set. Here's what waits for a yes, and who can give it.

## What waits for a yes

| What | Where you approve | Who can approve |
| - | - | - |
| A [Paid optimization](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/performance/optimizer.md) budget recommendation | **Paid Optimization → Actions**, or from your assistant | **Operator** or higher |
| A move [Jaina](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/performance/jaina.md) proposes — a new audience, creative angles, a creative slate, a pipeline run, or an Optimizer approval | In the chat with Jaina, on that exact action | You, in the chat |
| Creating or changing a Meta campaign, ad set, ad, budget, or audience from your assistant | Your assistant shows a preview and waits for your yes | **Operator** or higher |
| Switching on a paused campaign, ad set, or ad, or a large budget increase | In the Continuum app, or from an Admin's or Owner's own assistant with `mcp_approval_grant` | **Admin** or **Owner** |

New campaigns, ad sets, and ads are always created **paused**. The Optimizer never pauses anything without a person approving that specific pause.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Approvals are part of [Performance+](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/performance/overview.md). See [pricing](https://trycontinuum.ai/#pricing).

## Try it

In the app, go to **Paid Optimization → Actions**, open a recommendation, read its reasoning, and approve or reject it.

Or ask Claude or ChatGPT:

* "Show me this week's budget recommendations and explain each one."
* "Approve the recommendations for our prospecting campaigns, and reject the rest."
* "Show me the paid changes waiting for my approval." (Admins and Owners)

## What's next

* [Paid optimization](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/performance/optimizer.md): How budget recommendations are made and applied.
* [Roles & permissions](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/settings/roles.md): Control who can approve.

# Brand book

Source: https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/brand/overview

> The living, AI-generated identity that grounds every generation and agent in Continuum.

Your brand book is the single source of truth for how your brand looks, sounds, and shows up. Continuum drafts it from your website during onboarding and deepens it over time. It isn't just reference — it actively **grounds** [Canvas](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/canvas/skills-and-grounding.md) generations and steers the [agents](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/concepts.md), so your output stays on-brand by default.

## In this section

| Page | What it covers |
| - | - |
| [Set up your brand](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/brand/setup.md) | Build your brand profile from your website. |
| [Brand readiness](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/brand/readiness.md) | How complete your brand book is, and what would raise the score. |
| [Knowledge base](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/settings/knowledge.md) | The documents that feed your brand book and agents. |

## Where it lives

Open **Settings → Brand Intelligence**. Four scores sit at the top — identity readiness, evidence coverage, competitor coverage, and observed visibility — above six tabs:

| Tab | What it holds |
| - | - |
| **Overview** | The evidence behind your brand profile, and when it was last refreshed. |
| **Brand DNA** | Identity (color palette, typography, voice, personality, imagery, and content rules), strategy (positioning and audience), and the editable `brand.md`. |
| **Competition** | The competitors Continuum tracks for you, with their status and a strategic summary. |
| **Visibility** | A simulated estimate of how visible your brand is in AI answers. It's an estimate, not observed ChatGPT, Perplexity, or Google AI data. |
| **Readiness** | Your [brand readiness score](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/brand/readiness.md) and what would raise it. |
| **Sources** | The knowledge-base documents and onboarding intake behind the book. |

Below the tabs, the **design system** section holds the visual sources Continuum applies to creative.

## Brand kit

The brand kit is the deterministic core of your identity — the pieces any feature can pull by brand:

* **Logo** — your logo file.
* **Colors** — your brand palette as hex values.
* **Typography** — your brand typefaces, stored as font-family names.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Typography is stored as font names, not font files — Continuum references the families. (Client After Effects projects are the exception: those require the actual font files. See [After Effects delivery](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/forge/after-effects/delivery.md).)

## Generating and editing

If your brand book is empty, select **Generate Brand Book** to build it from your website and onboarding answers. Edit the **Authoritative brand document** — the `brand.md` under **Brand DNA** — to change what agents must follow. Derived intelligence never overwrites your edits.

## Working across brands

Each brand has its own brand book, kit, and connected accounts. Switch the **active brand** from the brand switcher to move between them, or create a new brand profile. A brand that hasn't finished onboarding or has no active integration is flagged so you know what to finish.

## Try it

Ask Claude or ChatGPT:

* "Read our brand book and tell me in three lines how we sound."
* "What does our brand book say about how we talk on LinkedIn?"
* "What are our brand colors, as hex values?"

## What's next

* [Brand readiness](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/brand/readiness.md): See how complete your brand book is.
* [Brand-book grounding](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/canvas/skills-and-grounding.md): How the brand book shapes generations.

# Set up your brand

Source: https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/brand/setup

> Build your brand profile from your website in a few minutes: analyze, connect channels, invite your team, and launch.

Continuum builds your brand from your website. You give it a URL, it scans your site to extract your brand identity, and you review and launch. The whole flow takes a few minutes.

**1. Enter your website**

Head to [app.trycontinuum.ai](https://app.trycontinuum.ai) and start onboarding. Enter your website URL and select **Analyze my brand**.

Continuum scans your site and starts an AI analysis in the background — extracting your name, logo, colors, typography, voice, and audience while you continue.

**2. Add brand documents (optional)**

Upload any brand assets you already have — style guides, decks, or past campaigns. This sharpens the analysis, but it's optional: skip it and Continuum infers everything from your website.

**3. Connect your channels**

Tag your ad and social accounts to this brand. Connect a provider once, then assign the specific accounts that belong to this brand.

* **Meta** — Facebook, Instagram, and your Meta ad accounts
* **TikTok**
* **YouTube**

Connecting Instagram unlocks competitor inspiration later. You can add more channels — including LinkedIn — anytime from **Settings → Integrations**. See [Integrations](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/integrations.md) for the full list.

**4. Invite your team (optional)**

Invite teammates and set each one's role — **Admin**, **Operator**, or **Viewer**. You can also do this later from Settings.

> [!TIP]
>
> Not sure which role to give? See [Roles & permissions](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/settings/roles.md).

**5. Review your Brand DNA and launch**

Continuum shows the brand profile it extracted — identity (logo, colors, typography), business overview, voice and tone, target audience, and a **brand readiness score**. Edit anything that's off, then launch.

The readiness score tells you how complete your brand profile is. It's informational — it never blocks you. You can deepen your [brand book](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/brand/overview.md) over time.

> [!NOTE]
>
> After you launch, Continuum can show competitor inspiration and generate your first on-brand creatives, then drop you on your Home dashboard.

## Try it

Already connected Claude or ChatGPT? Ask:

* "Create a new brand called Acme Coffee for example.com." You finish setting it up in the Continuum app.
* "Which Continuum brand am I working on, and what's connected?"
* "Connect our Instagram account."

## What's next

* [Core concepts](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/concepts.md): How brands, agents, and the creative loop fit together.
* [Build your brand book](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/brand/overview.md): Deepen the identity that grounds every generation.
* [AI Canvas](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/canvas/overview.md): Generate and edit images and video on the canvas.
* [Integrations](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/integrations.md): Connect and assign all your channels.

# Brand readiness

Source: https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/brand/readiness

> A 0–100 score of how complete your brand book is — informational, never a gate.

The brand readiness score tells you how complete and strong your [brand book](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/brand/overview.md) is. A more complete brand book gives the AI more to work with, so generations and agent output get sharper.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Readiness is **informational**. It measures your brand profile — it does **not** score individual creatives, and it never blocks you from generating, publishing, or launching.

## What it measures

The overall score runs 0–100 and breaks down into seven dimensions:

| Dimension | What it reflects |
| - | - |
| **Value prop** | How clearly your value proposition is defined. |
| **ICP clarity** | How well your ideal customer is described. |
| **Customer pains** | Whether the problems you solve are captured. |
| **Success metrics** | Whether you've defined what success looks like. |
| **Positioning** | How distinct and clear your positioning is. |
| **Messaging** | How coherent your messaging is. |
| **Identity** | How complete your visual and verbal identity is. |

Each dimension carries its own score and rationale, and the overall score maps to a band — **not started**, **needs work**, **developing**, or **ready**.

## Improving your score

* Fill in the gaps the low-scoring dimensions point to, directly in the [brand book](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/brand/overview.md).
* Add source material under **Settings → Knowledge** so the AI has more to draw on — see [Knowledge base](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/settings/knowledge.md).
* Select **Recalculate** to re-score after you make changes.

## Try it

1. Open **Settings → Brand Intelligence** and choose the **Readiness** tab.
2. Find your lowest dimension, such as **ICP clarity**.
3. Add a customer persona document under **Settings → Knowledge**, or ask your assistant: "Save this customer persona to our knowledge base."
4. Select **Recalculate**.

Or ask Claude or ChatGPT: "Read our brand book and tell me which parts look thin."

## What's next

* [Brand book](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/brand/overview.md): Fill the gaps readiness surfaces.
* [Knowledge base](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/settings/knowledge.md): Give the AI more source material.

# Knowledge base

Source: https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/settings/knowledge

> Upload the documents that ground your brand book, the agents, and Jaina.

The knowledge base is where you give Continuum source material about your brand and business. The documents you add here feed your [brand book](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/brand/overview.md), the [agents](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/concepts.md), and [Jaina](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/performance/jaina.md), so their output reflects what's actually true about you.

## What to add

Upload the documents that describe your brand and strategy — brand guidelines, positioning docs, product information, past campaigns, and research. The more grounded material Continuum has, the stronger your [brand readiness](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/brand/readiness.md) and the sharper every generation.

## Strategic analysis

From the knowledge base you can **run a strategic analysis** that synthesizes your documents into a consolidated brand guideline. This gives the agents a single, coherent reference instead of a pile of raw files.

## Try it

Ask Claude or ChatGPT:

* "Save this product FAQ so you can use it in future posts."
* "Add our About page at example.com/about to our knowledge base."
* "What does our knowledge base say about our return policy?"

To add a PDF or other file, upload it under **Settings → Knowledge** in the app. Saving material from your assistant needs the **Operator** role or higher; Viewers can read and search it.

## What's next

* [Brand book](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/brand/overview.md): See how knowledge shapes your identity.
* [Brand readiness](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/brand/readiness.md): Watch your score improve as you add sources.

# Integrations

Source: https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/integrations

> Connect your ad and social platforms once, then assign specific accounts to a brand.

Continuum uses a **connect once, assign to a brand** model. You connect a provider (like Meta) a single time at your account level, and Continuum discovers every asset you can access. You then assign the specific accounts — a Facebook Page, an Instagram profile, an ad account — to a given brand. Nothing syncs until you assign it, which keeps data from leaking between brands you manage.

## Supported channels

| Channel | What you get in Continuum |
| - | - |
| **Meta — Facebook** | Organic performance, plus your Meta ad accounts: campaign performance, creative, budgets, and reporting, with [Paid optimization](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/performance/optimizer.md) and campaign management on the same connection. |
| **Meta — Instagram** | Organic performance, competitor discovery, and [publishing](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/organic/publishing.md). |
| **LinkedIn** | Organic performance, and LinkedIn ads performance. Managing LinkedIn ads stays in LinkedIn for now. |
| **TikTok** | Organic performance. |
| **YouTube** | Organic channel performance. |

Instagram publishing is live. For Facebook, LinkedIn, TikTok, and YouTube, contact support before your first post on each, and the Continuum team publishes it with you. See [Publishing](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/organic/publishing.md).

## Connecting a channel

**1. Open Integrations**

Go to **Settings → Integrations** and choose the provider you want to connect, such as Meta, LinkedIn, TikTok, or YouTube.

**2. Authorize**

Complete the provider's OAuth flow in the popup. Continuum discovers every account and asset you can access — you don't authorize each one separately.

**3. Assign accounts to a brand**

Pick the specific accounts that belong to this brand and assign them. Assigning starts background data collection for that account.

## How Meta assets are organized

Meta nests deeply, so the asset picker mirrors its hierarchy: **Meta Business → ad accounts → sub-assets** (Pages and Instagram profiles). Selecting an ad account can surface the Instagram profiles tied to that business unit, so related assets stay together.

Assets that are discovered but not yet usable — for example, missing a permission — are flagged so you know what to fix before assigning them.

## Keeping connections healthy

Continuum tracks each connection's last sync and health. If a connection breaks — a password change or an expired token — the account is marked stale and shows a **Re-sync** action to restore data collection.

> [!NOTE]
>
> These are your ad and social platforms. AI assistants you've connected, such as Claude or ChatGPT, are listed under **Settings → Connections**. See [Connections and activity](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/settings/connections.md).

## Try it

Ask Claude or ChatGPT:

* "Which platforms are connected to our brand?"
* "Connect our Instagram account."
* "Is our Meta connection healthy?"

When you ask to connect, you get a link to approve the connection. It works for 10 minutes.

## What's next

* [Assign accounts to brands](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/brand/overview.md): Manage which assets belong to each brand.
* [Paid analytics](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/performance/analytics.md): See paid performance once Meta is connected.
* [Security & privacy](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/security.md): How access is controlled and revoked.

# Roles & permissions

Source: https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/settings/roles

> How brand and account scopes work, and what Owners, Admins, Operators, and Viewers can do.

Continuum settings are split into two scopes, and each teammate has a role that sets what they can do.

## Brand scope vs. account scope

* **Brand scope** — settings for the active brand: **Activation**, **General** (identity and members), **Brand Intelligence**, **Skills**, **Prompts**, **Integrations**, **Knowledge**, and **Billing**.
* **Account scope** — settings for you as a user: **Profile**, **Connections** (your connected AI assistants), **Activity**, **Brands**, **Notifications**, and **Drive**.

## Roles

Each member of a brand has one of these roles:

| Role | Broadly can |
| - | - |
| **Owner** | Everything an Admin can, as the brand's owner. |
| **Admin** | Manage the brand end to end, including members and billing. |
| **Operator** | Do the day-to-day work — create, generate, and publish. |
| **Viewer** | View the brand's work without making changes. |

> [!NOTE]
>
> The exact capabilities for each role are shown in the in-app role legend under **Settings → General**.

## Roles in your AI assistant

A connected assistant works as you, so your role on each brand applies there too.

| Role | From your assistant, can |
| - | - |
| **Viewer** | Read results, the content plan, the Library, the brand book, budget recommendations, pipelines, and Forge templates. |
| **Operator** | Also ask Jaina and the Organic agent; draft, approve, and publish posts; generate on the canvas and run pipelines; edit video; comment on and review Library work; save brand material; create and change Meta ads; approve or reject budget recommendations; and fill Forge templates. |
| **Admin**, **Owner** | Also approve switching on a campaign, ad set, or ad, or a large budget increase, with `mcp_approval_grant`; and produce final versions in [Forge](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/forge/overview.md). |

Some brands require an Admin or Owner to approve every publish and paid change. On those brands, an Operator's yes waits for that approval. See [You stay in control](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/mcp/control.md).

## Managing your team

Invite teammates and set their roles from **Settings → General**, or during [onboarding](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/quickstart.md). You can change a member's role or remove them later from the same place.

## Try it

* **Add a reviewer:** to let a freelancer see work without changing anything, go to **Settings → General**, invite them by email, such as "[freelancer@example.com](mailto:freelancer@example.com)", and choose **Viewer**.
* **Check your own role:** ask your assistant "What's my role on this brand?"
* **Approve a change as an Admin:** ask your assistant "Show me the paid changes waiting for my approval."

## What's next

* [Knowledge base](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/settings/knowledge.md): Give the AI shared source material.
* [Billing](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/settings/billing.md): Manage your plan and tier.

# Connections and activity

Source: https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/settings/connections

> See which AI assistants you've connected to Continuum, revoke any of them, and review every action you've taken through one.

When you connect Claude, ChatGPT, or another assistant to Continuum, two settings pages keep it accountable: one lists the connections, the other lists what they did.

## Connections

**Settings → Connections** lists every assistant you've connected to Continuum. Revoke any you no longer use. To use one again later, [connect it](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/quickstart.md#connect-your-assistant) and sign in once more.

> [!NOTE]
>
> These are AI assistant connections. Your social and ad platforms are managed separately under **Settings → Integrations**. See [Integrations](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/integrations.md).

## Activity

**Settings → Activity** lists every action you've taken through a connected assistant, and when. Each person sees their own activity.

Use it to check what an assistant did on your behalf. If something looks wrong, revoke the connection under **Settings → Connections** and contact [support@trycontinuum.ai](mailto:support@trycontinuum.ai).

## Try it

* **Check what an assistant did:** after you ask "Move Thursday's posts to Friday", open **Settings → Activity** and find that change, whether it worked, and when.
* **Clean up:** open **Settings → Connections**, find an assistant you've stopped using, such as "ChatGPT", and revoke it.

## What's next

* [You stay in control](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/mcp/control.md): What waits for your yes.
* [Roles & permissions](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/settings/roles.md): What each role can do from an assistant.

# Billing

Source: https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/settings/billing

> Manage each brand's plans, Canvas credits, payment method, and invoices.

Billing lives under **Settings → Billing** for the active brand. Each brand has its own plans and credits, so you can run brands at different levels.

## What's on the billing page

| Section | What it controls |
| - | - |
| **Plans** | Your Organic+ and Performance+ plans, which unlock those product lines. A plan whose charge didn't go through shows **Payment failed**. |
| **Canvas credits** | The balance that image, video, voiceover, and music generation draws from, and how much of it has been used this period. See [Providers and rates](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/providers-and-rates.md) for what each generation costs. |
| **Credit packs** | Top up Canvas credits with a one-time pack. Credits you buy never expire. |
| **Auto-billing** | Off unless you turn it on. When the brand runs out of Canvas credits, generation keeps going and usage is billed on your next invoice. Your credits and packs are used first. |
| **Payment method** and **Invoices** | Your card on file and past invoices. |

## When you run out of Canvas credits

Generation pauses for that brand until you buy a credit pack or turn on auto-billing.

> [!NOTE]
>
> For current plans and what each includes, see [pricing](https://trycontinuum.ai/#pricing).

## Try it

* **Check your balance before a big batch:** before you ask for "Make ten 8-second clips of our new product", go to **Settings → Billing** and read **Canvas credits**. Compare it with the rates in [Providers and rates](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/providers-and-rates.md).
* **Top up the right brand:** credits land on the active brand. Check that the brand switcher shows the brand you mean, such as "Acme Coffee", then go to **Settings → Billing → Credit packs**, choose a pack, and pay.
* **Keep generating at zero:** go to **Settings → Billing** and turn on **Auto-billing**.

When a brand runs out and auto-billing is off, the node shows "Out of Canvas credits" instead of generating.

## What's next

* [AI Canvas](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/canvas/overview.md): What your Canvas credits power.
* [Performance+](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/performance/overview.md): Paid media, on the Performance+ plan.
* [Providers and rates](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/providers-and-rates.md): What each generation costs in Canvas credits.

# Changelog

Source: https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/changelog

> Dated product and documentation updates for Continuum: new features, changed behavior, and new or rebuilt guides, newest first.

Notable product and documentation updates, newest first.

**November 2026**

Documentation

The [tool reference](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/mcp/tools.md) now covers every tool the connector lists, plus the ones it accepts by name. Each area page gives each tool's role, confirmation, inputs, an example call, and its errors, and agents can read it all as [JSON](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/mcp/tools.json). New: Forge [Figma import](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/forge/functions.md#forge_manage-source_figma), the per-action [confirmation lifetimes](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/mcp/reference.md#confirmations), and how an Admin or Owner [approves a change](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/mcp/control.md#what-waits-for-your-yes) from an assistant.

**October 2026**

Rates

New [Providers and rates](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/providers-and-rates.md) page: who makes each model and what each generation costs in Canvas credits. Generated voiceovers and music now use Canvas credits too. Google retired Veo 3.1, so Veo requests now run on Omni 1.1 Flash at Omni's rate.

**October 2026**

Documentation

Rebuilt the docs around using Continuum from your AI assistant. New guides cover [connecting Claude, ChatGPT, and Claude Code](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/quickstart.md#connect-your-assistant), [what you can do](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/mcp/overview.md), [prompt recipes](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/mcp/recipes.md), [what waits for your yes](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/mcp/control.md), and a [tool reference](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/mcp/tools.md). The product guides are now organized by product line: [Creative+](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/canvas/overview.md), [Organic+](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/organic/overview.md), and [Performance+](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/performance/overview.md). The site has a new look to match trycontinuum.ai.

**July 2026**

Documentation

Rebuilt the documentation to match the shipped product — new guides for the [AI Canvas](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/canvas/overview.md), [Organic+](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/organic/overview.md), [Performance+](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/performance/overview.md), [Brand](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/brand/overview.md), and [Brand Spy](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/brand/spy.md).

# Troubleshooting

Source: https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/troubleshooting

> Fixes for common problems, in two parts: your AI assistant and the connector (sign-in, brands, permissions, limits, jobs), and the Continuum app (integrations, data, plans, credits, the canvas).

Find your problem below. Each answer says what's happening and what to do.

## In your AI assistant

### I added the connector but can't see Continuum in my chat

Check the Continuum connector is switched on for this chat, or start a new chat. On a Claude Team or Enterprise plan, your organization owner may need to add the connector first.

### It can't find my brand

Ask "Which brands can I access?" If yours isn't listed, ask an Admin or Owner on that brand to invite you in Continuum.

### I'm not sure which accounts are connected

Ask "Which platforms are connected to our brand?" You can connect anything missing from the same chat.

### It asks me to pick a brand or connect an account

That's normal. Answer the question, or open the link it gives you. Links work for 10 minutes.

### An account won't connect, or a post can't be published

First ask "Is our Instagram connection healthy?" (or whichever platform). If the connection has lapsed, ask Continuum to reconnect it, or re-sync it in the app (see [In the app](#in-the-app)). If that platform doesn't support publishing from your assistant yet, Continuum says so. See [Good to know](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/mcp/limits.md).

### It says my brand isn't ready

Finish [setting up your brand](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/brand/setup.md) in the Continuum app so your brand book can be built, then try again. Until then, you can still connect your accounts and look at your performance.

### I'm not sure what the assistant just did

Open **Settings → Activity** in Continuum. It lists every action you've taken through your assistant, and when. If something looks wrong, revoke the connection under **Settings → Connections** and contact [support@trycontinuum.ai](mailto:support@trycontinuum.ai).

### It says I don't have permission

Your role doesn't allow that action. Viewers can read; asking Jaina or the Organic agent, and anything that creates, changes, or runs, needs Operator; switching on an ad needs an Admin or Owner. Ask an Admin or Owner on your brand. See [Roles & permissions](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/settings/roles.md).

### It says my session has expired

Remove the Continuum connector in your assistant's settings and add it again. You'll be asked to sign in to Continuum once more.

### ChatGPT won't finish signing in

Check you used the ChatGPT address: `https://api.trycontinuum.ai/mcp/chatgpt`.

### It says I've hit a limit

Bigger jobs, like generating creative, have hourly limits to protect your budget. Ask for a smaller batch, such as three versions instead of ten, or try again in about an hour. The message says how long to wait.

### It's taking a while

Answers and reports usually take a minute or two. Images and video can take several minutes. Ask "Is it done yet?" to check, or come back to the same chat later.

## In the app

### An integration shows as stale or disconnected

A connection goes stale when its token expires or the account password changes. Open **Settings → Integrations**, find the affected connection, and select **Re-sync** to restore data collection. See [Integrations](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/integrations.md).

### No data is showing in analytics

Data appears only for accounts you've **assigned** to the active brand. Connecting a provider isn't enough — assign the specific ad or social accounts to this brand under **Settings → Integrations**, then give background collection time to run.

### Performance+ or Organic+ is locked

Each product line is part of a plan. If one is locked, check the brand's plans under **Settings → Billing**. See [Billing](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/settings/billing.md) and [pricing](https://trycontinuum.ai/#pricing).

### Generation stopped on the canvas

The brand may be out of Canvas credits. Buy a credit pack or turn on auto-billing under **Settings → Billing**. See [Billing](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/settings/billing.md).

### Brand Spy has no competitor posts

Tracking a competitor's organic posts relies on Instagram data. Connect an Instagram account in [Integrations](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/integrations.md), then add competitors in Brand Spy's **Competitors** tab. See [Brand Spy](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/brand/spy.md).

### My brand book looks thin or empty

If your brand book is empty, open **Settings → Brand Intelligence** and select **Generate Brand Book** to build it from your website. Improve it over time by filling gaps and adding documents to your [knowledge base](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/settings/knowledge.md), then recalculate your [readiness score](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/brand/readiness.md).

### A canvas node won't run

A generation node runs only once every input it depends on has valid data. Check that upstream nodes show **Done**, that required connections are made, and that you've selected a model. A node that failed shows **Error**. See [Working on the canvas](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/canvas/working-on-the-canvas.md).

## Still stuck?

Email [support@trycontinuum.ai](mailto:support@trycontinuum.ai). For an assistant problem, say which assistant you use and what you asked.

## What's next

* [Connect your assistant](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/quickstart.md#connect-your-assistant): Set up the connector again, step by step.
* [Integrations](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/integrations.md): Connect, assign, and re-sync accounts.
* [Good to know](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/mcp/limits.md): Current limits by area.
* [Billing](https://docs.trycontinuum.ai/settings/billing.md): Plans, Canvas credits, and auto-billing.
